subject.size_in_frame: head and upper body large in the near foreground, face about 0.20 of frame height

second_subject.note: upright in the upper third with the book — the water-side camera faces east, so the sister's northern sitting place falls screen left.

headroom: the sister keeps about 0.10 of frame height of leaf shade above her; Alice, rolled onto her back in the near foreground, has none — her crown runs out of the right edge at eye height.
horizon_eyeline: Far bank grass line at 0.22 of frame height. The sister's eyeline stays down on her page; Alice's turns up out of the top of frame to the elm leaves and then closes.

layers.fg: Alice's face and shoulder, and the single daisy dropping onto her pinafore in the lower right corner
layers.mg: the flattened grass of the shelf between them, daisies in the turf
layers.bg: the sister upright with the book, the elm trunk behind her, the shaded bank beyond

gaze.note: Alice rolls onto her back and her look goes straight up out of frame into the canopy; the lead room is the strip of leaf shade along the top edge. The sister never looks up, so the two eyelines never meet — the hush is delivered to someone who is not being looked at.

balance: A long diagonal see-saw from the small upright sister at top left to the large recumbent Alice at bottom right. Big-near versus small-far keeps the frame from settling for all eleven seconds.
leading_lines: The slope of the bank runs from lower right to upper left and ties the two figures together; the sister's vertical spine and the elm trunk are the only uprights, and they hold the far end of that diagonal.
eye_first: Alice's face large in the near foreground, then along the bank slope up to the sister and the page, then back down to the falling daisy.
constraint_binding: One take, no move, single pick-and-drop: the daisy is picked and dropped within one frame with no reframe onto the hand, and no weighing sequence is staged — the whole comparison happens in one wide composition.
